assessments.reasoning: The 8.3.27 type section distinguishes a value's fixed type from the types of values a variable can refer to. The variable section scopes implicit declaration to first left-hand assignment and rejects using a previously undeclared variable in expressions.
The Russian article says the variable's type follows its current value. This corroborates the general dynamic model without fixing the exact 8.3.27 implicit-declaration rule.

challenge.method: Compare assigning two value types to the same variable, changing a mutable object without changing its type, and using a previously undeclared name on the right side. Contrast the broader Russian overview and the independently implemented OneScript runtime.
challenge.results: A variable can come to refer to a value of another type while each value keeps its type. The implicit declaration permits the specified first left-hand assignment; it does not license a first read of an undeclared name. The Russian overview corroborates the broader dynamic view and does not document the exact declaration rule.

limitations: The claim is a source-level typing and declaration description for 8.3.27. The exact conclusions leave storage representation, object mutability and runtime compatibility to separate evidence.
